channel.title: Merkle Street
channel.description: Merkle Street reports crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, layer 2s, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation, security incidents and protocol upgrades.

item.title: Check a BSC Token Contract Before You Swap
item.description: A BSC token swap calls a contract through a pool, so check the address, verified code, owner permissions, liquidity and token approval before signing a transaction.

item.title: How to Track Cost Basis Across a Crypto Bridge
item.description: A bridge moves assets across ledgers, but the record must connect both sides; that link lets you preserve cost basis and separate transfers from disposals.

item.title: Moving Mantle sale proceeds to Ethereum for a tax reserve
item.description: A Mantle sale can create a tax liability before the cash reaches Ethereum; bridge the proceeds, keep fee and transaction records, and reserve the amount your local rules require.

item.title: Mantle Bridge Moves App Funds Between Ethereum and Mantle
item.description: Mantle Bridge moves ETH, MNT and tokens between Ethereum and Mantle; learn how deposits and withdrawals work, and what to check before using an app.

item.title: Bridge the Amount a Manta Payment Needs
item.description: Bridge only the asset and amount the payment needs, reserve native gas on both networks, and check the asset, network and return route before signing.

item.title: How to Check a Bridge Contract in a Network Explorer
item.description: Check a bridge contract in a network explorer to match its address, code and transaction history to the right network before authorizing a transfer.

item.title: What a Bridge Upgrade Notice Means for Long-Term Holdings
item.description: A bridge upgrade notice can change where a transfer is sent or how it is verified; long-term holders should check the route, deadline and withdrawal path.

item.title: How Much Crypto Should You Send From Your Wallet?
item.description: Send the recipient’s exact amount, then check that your wallet can also pay the network fee and preserve any balance you need for later transactions.

item.title: How Treasury Teams Reconcile Cross-Chain Swaps
item.description: Cross-chain swaps settle across separate ledgers, so treasury teams must match the instruction, source debit, route status and destination receipt before closing the books.

item.title: A Token’s Ticker Is Not Its Identity
item.description: A token’s ticker is not enough to identify it: check its network, contract address, and destination before sending or swapping funds, so you can distinguish assets that share a familiar name.

item.title: The account a first token swap may need to create
item.description: A token account gives a wallet a place to hold a specific asset; learn why a swap may create one, add a setup cost, and change the transaction you approve.

item.title: What Makes a Liquidity Pool Resilient After a Price Gap
item.description: A pool survives a price gap when its remaining liquidity can absorb arbitrage trades without excessive slippage, and fees or rebalancing can restore useful depth.

item.title: How to Compare Swap Routes with byreal
item.description: Compare a swap route by checking the amount received, the pools and hops it uses, and execution risk; a quoted path is useful only when its costs are clear.

item.title: How to Pay Contributors From a Treasury on Another Chain
item.description: A cross-chain contributor payout starts with a treasury policy, then moves approved funds through a bridge or liquidity route before recipients claim or receive payment.

item.title: How Destination Liquidity Works in Wallet Transfers
item.description: Destination liquidity lets a transfer finish when a provider pays tokens on the receiving chain; the source settles later, with fees and inventory shaping the route.

item.title: Four stages route DEX rewards to trading pairs
item.description: DEX rewards reach selected trading pairs through emissions, veBLACK votes and gauges; only liquidity staked in a pool’s gauge earns its emissions.

item.title: How to prepare a missing deposit asset
item.description: A missing deposit asset can mean an empty balance, hidden token, or unsupported route; identify which one before adding funds, approving a contract, or swapping.

item.title: Swap the Right Amount Before Funding a New Token Pair
item.description: Swap only the token amount needed for the pair’s target ratio, then add both assets to the pool and check the initial on-chain price before confirming.

item.title: When AMM Fees Cover Impermanent Loss
item.description: AMM fees offset impermanent loss only when your share of trading fees exceeds the pool’s value gap against holding the same tokens, after costs.

item.title: Base swap: four checks before trading or adding liquidity
item.description: Before using a Base swap, check the token address, pool depth, price impact and liquidity risks; each changes what a trade or deposit can actually deliver.
